feat(composition): preserve hints on composition failure (#9305)

Previously, when composition failed (either during merge or satisfiability validation), all WARN-level hints were silently discarded because the error type `Vec<CompositionError>` had no room for them.

Introduce `CompositionFailure { errors, hints }` as the error type for `merge_subgraphs`, `validate_satisfiability`, `compose`, and related functions. This preserves `INCONSISTENT_*` warnings, `UNUSED_ENUM_TYPE`, `OVERRIDDEN_FIELD_CAN_BE_REMOVED`, and other hints alongside errors on all failure paths:

- `merge_subgraphs`: carries merge hints when merge produces errors
- `validate_satisfiability`: carries accumulated hints when satisfiability fails
- `validate_satisfiability_with_connectors`: merges hints from both merge and satisfiability phases, sanitizes connector names in both
- `compose` / `compose_with_connectors`: propagates hints through the full pipeline; pre-merge phases (no hints) convert via `From<Vec<CompositionError>>`

xtask: isolate `release new` in a git worktree + style the UX

Two structural changes to `cargo xtask release new`:

1. **WorkTree isolation.**  All destructive git ops (branch creation,
   empty-commit shim, push) now run inside an isolated `git worktree`
   sibling to the project root.  The user's primary checkout HEAD,
   index, and working tree are NOT touched.  Concurrent runs each get
   their own worktree — no race on shared .git/index state.

   New helper at `xtask/src/worktree.rs`:
   - `WorkTree::create(path, base_ref)` — creates the worktree.
   - `.git(args)` / `.git_out(args)` — run git inside it.
   - Drop impl removes the worktree (`git worktree remove --force`).
   - `.keep()` opts out of cleanup for post-mortem debugging.

   New flags on `release new`:
   - `--keep-worktree` — keep the worktree directory on success.
     (Auto-kept on failure regardless, so the user can investigate.)
   - `--worktree-path <path>` — override the default sibling location.

2. **UX polish matching changeset's style.**

   - `version` arg is now optional.  Bare `cargo xtask release new`
     drops into a `dialoguer::Select` prompt: Patch / Minor / Major /
     Specific version (with Input prompt for the latter).
     Non-interactive run still requires the arg.
   - Plan block uses `console::style` (cyan version + branches, dim
     labels, bold version) instead of a single inline summary line.
   - Dry-run output is sectioned: fetch, worktree creation, in-worktree
     ops, PR open, cleanup — easier to follow the actual sequence.
   - Cheap validations (line, kind) happen BEFORE the fetch network
     call, so a misconfigured invocation errors instantly.

fix(federation): fix @fromContext positions for join__field (#9374)

`@fromContext` is applied to field **arguments**, so `DirectiveReferencers` stores them in `object_field_arguments` / `interface_field_arguments`. However, `needs_join_field` checks `object_fields` / `interface_fields`, causing it to miss fields that need `@join__field` with `contextArguments`.

When a field with `@fromContext` exists in all subgraphs with the same return type and no other special directives, `needs_join_field` incorrectly returned false, dropping the `@join__field` directive entirely—including the `contextArguments` data needed at runtime.

The fix maps argument positions to their parent field positions in `get_fields_with_from_context_directive`, matching the JS implementation:

```js
    // composition-js/src/merging/merge.ts:4037 — getFieldsWithFromContextDirective
    const field = application.parent.parent; // argument → field
```

https://github.com/apollographql/federation/blob/main/composition-js/src/merging/merge.ts#L4033-L4042

fix(composition): filter fake externals to only field-level `@external` (#9373)

`collect_fake_externals` traverses compound `@key` field sets (e.g., `@key(fields: "t { id }")`) and adds all reached fields to `fake_external_fields`. When a type stub uses type-level `@external` (e.g., `type T @key(fields: "id") @external { id: ID! }`), the traversal reaches `T.id` and incorrectly marks it as fake-external. This cancels out `fields_on_external_types` in `is_external()`, causing `needs_join_field()` to return false and drop all `@join__field` directives — including `external: true` — from the supergraph.

The JS implementation filters the traversal result:

```js
    collectTargetFields({...})
      .filter((field) => field.hasAppliedDirective(this.externalDirective))
      .forEach((field) => this.fakeExternalFields.add(field.coordinate));

    // federation/internals-js/src/federation.ts — collectFakeExternals, line 2709
    // https://github.com/apollographql/federation/blob/main/internals-js/src/federation.ts#L2709
```

The Rust `collect_fake_externals` was missing this filter — it added all fields from `collect_target_fields_from_field_set` unconditionally.

The fix adds `.filter(|field| external_fields.contains(field))` to only include fields that have field-level `@external` applied directly, matching the JS behavior.

fix(composition): interface cannot be a subtype of a union (#9382)

Union can only reference objects. While it is possible for a subgraph to define an `@interfaceObject` in the schema, in the merged supergraph it would still be represented as interface in the supergraph. `union_type.members` will never contain the target `interface` so the check would never succeed. `apollo-compiler` correctly validates this so we wouldn't generate invalid schema.

This PR cleans this incorrect logic but it should have no effect on the merged supergraph (this check would always fail).

Allowing unions to include interfaces/other unions is an old issue (https://github.com/graphql/graphql-spec/issues/711) and it looks like it won't be tackled anytime soon.

fix(composition): remove invalid executable directive from supergraph  (#9387)

When an executable directive has no locations common to all subgraphs, the JS composition removes it from the supergraph and returns early. The Rust implementation reported the hint but left the directive in the supergraph with zero locations and continued merging its properties.

This adds `dest.remove()` and an early return to match the JS behavior, preventing an invalid directive definition with empty locations from appearing in the supergraph.

fix(composition): fix `@interfaceObject` type kind mismatch (#9393)

`add_types_shallow` used `TypeDefinitionPosition` (a kind-carrying enum) as keys in `mismatched_types` and `subgraphs_with_interface_obj`. When a non-`@interfaceObject` subgraph was processed first, the merged schema stored `Object("Foo")` but the `@interfaceObject` map was keyed by `Interface("Foo")`, causing two lookup failures:

1. `.get()` for label lookup failed — `@interfaceObject` subgraphs were mislabeled as plain "Object Type" in `TYPE_KIND_MISMATCH` errors
2. `.contains()` for error suppression failed — a spurious `INTERFACE_OBJECT_USAGE_ERROR` was emitted

Fix: change both `mismatched_types` and `subgraphs_with_interface_obj` to use `Name` (plain type name) as keys, matching JS which uses `Set<string>` for both `mismatchedTypes` (L839) and `typesWithInterfaceObject` (L840):
https://github.com/apollographql/federation/blob/main/composition-js/src/merging/merge.ts#L838-L863

Also add early bail after `add_types_shallow` when errors exist, since type kind mismatches leave the merged schema in an inconsistent state that causes later stages to fail with internal errors that swallow the real `TYPE_KIND_MISMATCH` errors. JS avoids this by filtering mismatched types in `subgraphsTypes()` (L954-L957):
https://github.com/apollographql/federation/blob/main/composition-js/src/merging/merge.ts#L944-L961

JS `reportMismatchedTypeDefinitions` checks `isInterfaceObjectType()` directly on each source type (L929) rather than relying on a separate map lookup:
https://github.com/apollographql/federation/blob/main/composition-js/src/merging/merge.ts#L925-L942

fix(composition): drop `= {}` default when presence is inconsistent (#9389)

The Rust merger incorrectly preserved empty object defaults (`= {}`) when only some subgraphs declared them. JS composition drops the default in this case — an argument can only be optional in the supergraph if it is optional in all subgraphs.

Removes `inconsistent_defaults_are_all_coercible_empty_objects` and its special hint branch, aligning the condition with JS: `if (!isInconsistent || isIncompatible)`.

JS reference: `mergeDefaultValue` in `merge.ts`
https://github.com/apollographql/federation/blob/d4969572/composition-js/src/merging/merge.ts#L2412-L2413

fix(composition): add early return in `hint_on_inconsistent_value_type_field` (#9395)

`hint_on_inconsistent_value_type_field` was missing a `break` after emitting the hint. Since `report_mismatch_hint` already examines all sources internally, the loop emitted duplicate identical hints — one per subgraph missing the field.

JS breaks immediately after the first match (L1218): https://github.com/apollographql/federation/blob/main/composition-js/src/merging/merge.ts#L1189-L1221

fix(composition): Add early return in `hint_on_inconsistent_output_enum_value` (#9394)

`hint_on_inconsistent_output_enum_value` was missing a `return` after emitting the hint. Since `report_mismatch_hint` already examines all sources internally, the loop emitted duplicate identical hints — one per subgraph missing the value.

JS returns immediately after the first match (L2732): https://github.com/apollographql/federation/blob/main/composition-js/src/merging/merge.ts#L2713-L2735

The existing comment on L260 ("As soon as we find a subgraph that has the type but not the member, we hint") already described the intended behavior — the `return` was simply missing.

fix(composition): emit fallback `SubgraphLocation` when AST has no source (#9436)

`Subgraph::node_locations` returned an empty `Vec` when a schema node lacked AST source location data (common after programmatic schema modifications during the upgrade step). This caused `report_mismatch` to omit subgraphs from the `locations` array, leading to incorrect `maybe_prepend_subgraph` prefix behavior.

With only one subgraph in locations, a `[subgraph]` prefix was added to the message; JS included all subgraphs (2+), so no prefix was added. The message bodies were identical but the prefix differed.

Now `node_locations` produces a fallback `SubgraphLocation` with a default range (`0:0..0:0`) when no source data exists, matching JS behavior. This resolves mismatches in `INCONSISTENT_ENTITY`, `INCONSISTENT_INTERFACE_VALUE_TYPE_FIELD`, and
`INCONSISTENT_OBJECT_VALUE_TYPE_FIELD` hints.

fix(composition): populate `locations` for override-related hints (#9435)

Override hints (`OVERRIDDEN_FIELD_CAN_BE_REMOVED`, `OVERRIDE_DIRECTIVE_CAN_BE_REMOVED`, `OVERRIDE_MIGRATION_IN_PROGRESS`) were emitted with empty `locations`, causing a mismatch with the JS composer which populates the subgraph name. This led to `maybe_prepend_subgraph` producing different message prefixes between the two implementations.

Populate `SubgraphLocation` for all five override hint sites, using `subgraph_name` (the subgraph carrying `@override`) for `OverrideDirectiveCanBeRemoved` and `source_subgraph_name` (the overridden subgraph) for `OverriddenFieldCanBeRemoved` and `OverrideMigrationInProgress`, matching JS behavior.

fix(composition): add fallback location to `Node<T>` HasLocations impl (#9444)

`Node<T>::locations()` returned an empty `Vec` when a node lacked source location data, which happens when a subgraph defines a type via `extend type` without a base definition — the compiler creates a synthetic node with no `SourceSpan`. This caused `report_mismatch` to silently drop those subgraphs from hint locations.

#9436 fixed the analogous issue in `Subgraph::node_locations()`, but that code path is used by position-based `HasLocations` impls. When `report_mismatch` receives `Node<T>` values directly (e.g., from `merge_entities`), it uses the `Node<T>` impl which still lacked the fallback.

Compiler fix to populate location data -> https://github.com/apollographql/apollo-rs/pull/1041

fix(composition): expand default values in argument merger (#9454)

The argument merger in `merge_applied_directive` was using `specified_argument_by_name` which only returns explicitly specified arguments, skipping default values. This caused the merger to receive fewer values than the JS implementation which uses `arguments(true)` to expand defaults. fix(composition): preserve default value literals without expansion (#9451)

Stop `coerce_value()` from injecting type-level field defaults into partial input object literals during schema-level composition. Previously, a default like `{paging: {limit: 10}, sorting: []}` would be expanded to include absent fields (e.g. `inStock: true`), diverging from the subgraph's authored intent.

Introduce `DefaultValueBehavior` enum (`Expand` / `Check`) so the same `coerce_value()` function serves both contexts:
- `Check` (schema-level): validates the literal but preserves it as written — used by `coerce_schema_default_values`, `coerce_arguments_default_values_keep_empty_object`, and related schema/AST paths.
- `Expand` (executable-document): injects missing fields from type-level defaults — used by `coerce_operation_values`, `coerce_selection_set_values`, and directive application values on executable documents.

perf(composition): reduce allocations in hot paths (~8-10% faster) (#9480)

Three targeted optimizations to reduce unnecessary work during composition:

- Change `FederationSchema::get_type`/`try_get_type` to take `&Name` instead of owned `Name`, eliminating ~120 unnecessary `Arc<str>` clone/drop cycles
- Make `try_get_type` the primary implementation returning `Option`, so the `format!` error string is only allocated on actual lookup failures
- Add `Arc::ptr_eq` short-circuit to `ExcludedDestinations::eq`, skipping O(n²) content comparison when both sides share the same allocation

Benchmarked with a large (~320K line) supergraph: median composition time improved ~8.9%.

docs: log operations that exceed a candidate operation limit (#9294)

Adds a new "Logging operations that exceed a candidate limit" subsection to the request limits docs, showing how to use a custom telemetry event with a `gt` condition on the `query` selector to log operations that would exceed a candidate `max_aliases`, `max_depth`, `max_height`, or `max_root_fields` value — without configuring `limits` or enabling `warn_only` mode.  The example captures the client name and version from the `apollographql-client-name` and `apollographql-client-version` headers so teams can see which clients are sending the offending operations. fix(composition): Prune redundant join fields (#8744)

When applying `@join__field`, the `Merger` tries to limit applications to those where it adds information to the supergraph. When a field does not have `@join__field`, it is assumed to be present in all subgraphs. There are some cases where we add more applications than necessary. Instead of of changing the merge logic to be more selective, we can prune the schema after all merges are complete to remove this pattern. This specifically filters out `@join__field` applications when a field has `@join__field` for all subgraphs, and there is no other information (type, requires, etc) encoded in those `@join__field` applications.

fix(composition): restrict usage of auth directives on interfaces (#8826)

Restricts usage of `@authenticated`, `@policy` and `@requiresScopes` from being applied on interfaces, interface objects and their fields.

GraphQL spec currently does not define any interface inheritance rules and developers have to explicitly redefine all interface fields on their implementations. At runtime, GraphQL servers cannot return abstract types and always return concrete output types. Due to the above, applying auth directives on the interfaces may lead to unexpected runtime behavior as they won't have any effect at runtime.

fix(composition): fix directive arg merging logic (#8878)

Update `merge_applied_directives` to explicitly compare directive application arguments (accounting for default argument values) without modifying original directive. Previous logic was explicitly modifying original directive application and always populating it with default arg values even if they were not specified by the user, i.e. given a subgraph

```graphql
type Query {
  foo: String @deprecated
}
```

We expect the supergraph to also define it as

```graphql
type Query {
  # previous logic was applying @deprecated(reason: "No longer supported")
  foo: String @deprecated
}
```

fix(composition): enforce transitive auth requirements (#8870)

Adds new `validate_transitive_access_control_requirements_in_the_supergraph` post merge validation check to ensure that all fields that depends on data from other parts of the supergraph through `@requires` and/or `@fromContext` directives explicitly specify matching `@authenticated`, `@requiresScopes` and/or `@policy` auth requirements, e.g.

```graphql
type T @key(fields: "id") {
  id: ID!
  extra: String @external
  # we need explicit @authenticated as it is needed to access extra
  requiresExtra: String @requires(fields: "extra") @authenticated
}

type T @key(fields: "id") {
  id: ID!
  extra: String @authenticated
}
```

fix(composition): fixed merging interface object fields (#8906)

Interface fields and `@interfaceObject` fields should be merged using regular logic.

* fixed `add_fields_shallow` logic to correctly handle `@interfaceObject` fields for interfaces (previously if an `@interfaceObject` was found in the subgraph we would skip processing that subgraph altogether)
* fixed `add_missing_interface_object_fields_to_implementations` to only propagate `@interfaceObject` fields to objects if they don't declare those fields (otherwise they would already be merged accordingly, interface fields are already merged)
* added missing filtering of arg directives on `@interfaceObject` field to object fields propagation
* fixed `validate_override` logic
* fixed `validate_field_sharing` logic to use correct source
* fixed `add_missing_interface_object_fields_to_implementations` to invoke field sharing validation for propagate fields 
* also fixed the merge order of types to match JS

feat(composition): propagate access control directives to/from abstract types (#8914)

Updates composition merge logic to propagate access control directives
* upwards from object types to interface types
* upwards from object fields to interface fields fields
* upwards from interface object fields to other interface fields
* downwards from interface object fields to object fields

fix(composition): provide better error message for interface objects (#8917)

While GraphQL supports interfaces implementing other interfaces, this is currently unsupported when using `@interfaceObject`.

Updates `add_missing_interface_object_fields_to_implementations` logic to verify that we don't have any interface implementing `@interfaceObject`s interface and log more specific `INTERFACE_OBJECT_USAGE_ERROR` message if we do (previously composition would fail with misleading `INTERFACE_FIELD_NO_IMPLEM`).

fix(composition): handle missing directive definitions for older fed versions (#9229)

`SpecDefinition::directive_definition()` errors when a directive name resolves through the federation link prefix but the definition doesn't exist in the schema. This happens for directives added in newer federation versions (e.g. `@policy` in v2.6, `@fromContext` in v2.8) when subgraphs use an older version like v2.5.

The JS implementation avoids this by returning a stub with empty `applications()` from `getPost20FederationDirective`. The Rust code now uses `directive_name_in_schema` with a soft lookup in `directive_definitions`, gracefully skipping directives that don't exist in the subgraph schema.

fix(to-api-schema): Revert reorder of searching for imports vs fully qualified names when computing source feature (#9244)

In #9164, the code for `source_link_of_type()` and `source_link_of_directive()` was changed to be more in line with the JS equivalent `sourceFeature()`. As part of that, the methods were altered to attempt parsing the name as a fully qualified name before attempting to search through imports, as the JS code does. In JS these functions are only really used by composition, and flipping the order did cause a previously-ignored Rust composition test (ported from JS) to start passing.

However, in Rust, the `source_link_of_type()` and `source_link_of_directive()` are **_not_** only used by composition; the `to_api_schema()` function uses both of these methods (and in doing so, diverges from the JS implementation). And for the Rust implementation to properly handle specific edge cases around imports, it needs `source_link_of_type()` and `source_link_of_directive()` to search for imports before parsing the name as a fully qualified name.

So this PR reverts specifically just the ordering change made in #9164 to imports vs fully qualified names (the rest of the fixes in that PR remain in effect). Part of that means re-ignoring the aforementioned composition test; this will be fixed in a later PR.

xtask: add `release status` and `release reconcile` (milestone 1)

Adds two new `cargo xtask release` subcommands that read release state
from git remotes + GitHub and automate the most mechanical piece of the
flow (the reconcile-main-back-to-dev PR).  The RELEASE_CHECKLIST.md
stays as the "star map" documenting what the xtask does and serves as
the manual escape hatch when tooling is unavailable.

## `cargo xtask release status`

Read-only state detector.  Groups branches into release lines (tip =
plain `main`/`dev`, LTS = `main-v<MAJ>.<MIN>.x` + `dev-v<MAJ>.<MIN>.x`
pairs), attributes version branches/tags/PRs to the right line, and
prints a per-line snapshot of in-flight work.  Flags: `--repo`,
`--origin`, `--line`, `--json`, `--no-fetch`, `--non-interactive`.

## `cargo xtask release reconcile --version <X.Y.Z>`

Automates RELEASE_CHECKLIST.md §Reconciling steps 1-9.  Infers the
release line from `--line` or the current git branch (falls back to
interactive prompt).  Creates `reconcile-v<VERSION>`, merges line-dev
into it with a pre-seeded commit message (so no-conflict and
with-conflict paths both produce valid commits), pushes, opens the PR,
and sets auto-merge.  On merge conflicts it stops with instructions to
resolve locally and re-run with `--resume`.  Also supports
`--no-auto-merge` and `--dry-run`.

## Shared infrastructure

- `xtask/src/gh.rs` — consolidated `gh` CLI helper (`available`,
  `token`, `run`, `json`).  Extracted from ad-hoc calls in
  `changeset/mod.rs`; that module is migrated to consume the shared
  helper in the same change.
- `xtask/src/lib.rs` — new `git\!` and `git_out\!` macros matching the
  existing `cargo\!` / `npm\!` pattern.
- `xtask/src/commands/release/` — old `release.rs` split into
  `mod.rs`, `common.rs` (shared args + branch/line parsing),
  `prepare.rs`, `pre_verify.rs`, `state.rs` (detection), `status.rs`,
  `reconcile.rs`.

## LTS/security support is first-class from day one

Every subcommand accepts `--repo` (target GitHub repo, for private
forks), `--origin` (git remote), and `--line` (tip or
`<MAJ>.<MIN>.x`).  The `Line` type + branch-name regex are the single
source of truth for "which main/dev pair are we talking about" —
versions and tags are attributed back to lines automatically.

## RELEASE_CHECKLIST.md

Points readers to `release status` at the top of §Building a Release
and to `release reconcile` at the top of §Reconciling.  All manual
steps stay as-is — they're what the xtask runs under the hood.

Plan: plans/so-like-we-should-mellow-hollerith.md

xtask: recognize pre-release staging lines + --no-fetch warning

Follow-ups surfaced from running `release status` against real router
state.

## Staging line support (`dev-v3.x`)

Adds a new `Line::Staging { major }` variant alongside Tip and Lts.
Matches `main-v<MAJ>.x` / `dev-v<MAJ>.x` branches — a pre-release line
for a future major before any minor has been chosen.  Typical shape:
solo dev branch (`dev-v3.x`) accepting alpha releases, no main
counterpart yet because no release has shipped.

Also widens `--line` flag accepts `3.x`, version attribution splits
claims correctly between Tip/Staging/Lts (a 2.10.5 tag belongs to the
2.10.x LTS; a 3.0.0-alpha.0 tag belongs to the 3.x staging line; a
2.15.0 tag belongs to tip because nothing else claims 2.15).

## --no-fetch staleness warning

When `status --no-fetch` is passed against a stale clone, the tool used
to quietly report "no in-progress" for lines that actually had active
PRs.  Now prints a header reminder:

  Release state — apollographql/router (origin)
    (local state — did not `git fetch`; pass without --no-fetch for fresh data)

Easy to miss if you're running in CI; loud enough to notice interactively.

## JSON output

Adds `is_staging` field alongside existing `is_lts`.

fix(composition): prevent EnumTypeUsage from downgrading Both to Input/Output (#9303)

The `track_enum_usage` match arms for `Input | Both` and `Output | Both` incorrectly collapsed the `Both` variant back to a single-position usage whenever a subsequent field referenced the same enum in an already-seen position. For example, the sequence Input → Both → Output (third field) would overwrite `Both` with `Output`, silently skipping ENUM_VALUE_MISMATCH validation for enums used in both input and output contexts.

The JS composer (`merge.ts:2206`) handles this correctly: once position reaches `'Both'`, the expression `existing.position !== thisPosition` is always true, so `Both` is preserved.

The fix adds an explicit early match arm that returns `Both` unchanged, and removes the `| Both` alternatives from the `Input` and `Output` arms. This aligns RS behavior with JS for ~1,800 real-world supergraphs from the federation performance harness (groups 3.8 and 3.9).

xtask: add `release new` command for cutting fresh release branches

Cuts a new release branch from the line-appropriate base, opens the
draft release PR with the `release` label, and handles the empty-commit
shim conditionally (only when HEAD has no diff vs the line's main).

Per-line behavior:

- Tip patch         → cut from latest release tag (e.g., v2.14.0).  Dev
                      typically has post-release work that shouldn't
                      ship in a patch.
- Tip minor / major → cut from `dev`.
- LTS patch         → cut from line-dev (e.g., dev-v2.10.x), since LTS
                      dev IS the locked-down maintenance trunk.
- Staging line      → cut from line-dev (e.g., dev-v3.x).

Override base with `--from <commitish>`.  Override version with a
specific semver instead of `patch`/`minor`/`major`.

`--dry-run` prints the exact git/gh commands without executing.  The
PR body includes a Mergify-backport note pointing at the
`backport-<version>` label.

fix(composition): emit schema definition in supergraph SDL (#9359)

When subgraphs use `extend schema { query: Query }`, the merger preserved the extension origin on root operation `ComponentNames`, causing the serializer to emit `extend schema` blocks in the supergraph. Re-parsing this SDL then failed with `duplicate definitions for the query root operation type` because implicit root types from `Query`/`Mutation` type names conflicted with the extension.

Fixed merger to create fresh `ComponentNames` with `Definition` origin.

fix(composition): fix `EXTENSION_WITH_NO_BASE` validation (#9357)

The `EXTENSION_WITH_NO_BASE` check only detected orphan extensions using `extend type` syntax but missed types declared with the fed1 `@extends` directive (e.g., `type Product @key(fields: "id") @extends`). When all subgraphs used `@extends` with no base definition, the upgrader and merger incorrectly treated them as base types, silently succeeding instead of reporting the error.

Fix both `SchemaUpgrader::pre_upgrade_validations` and `Merger::check_for_extension_with_no_base` to also check for the `@extends` directive via `extends_directive_name()`, matching the JS implementation's `isFederationTypeExtension` which checks `hasAppliedDirective(metadata.extendsDirective())`.

JS reference:

xtask: isolate `release new` in a git worktree + style the UX

Two structural changes to `cargo xtask release new`:

1. **WorkTree isolation.**  All destructive git ops (branch creation,
   empty-commit shim, push) now run inside an isolated `git worktree`
   sibling to the project root.  The user's primary checkout HEAD,
   index, and working tree are NOT touched.  Concurrent runs each get
   their own worktree — no race on shared .git/index state.

   New helper at `xtask/src/worktree.rs`:
   - `WorkTree::create(path, base_ref)` — creates the worktree.
   - `.git(args)` / `.git_out(args)` — run git inside it.
   - Drop impl removes the worktree (`git worktree remove --force`).
   - `.keep()` opts out of cleanup for post-mortem debugging.

   New flags on `release new`:
   - `--keep-worktree` — keep the worktree directory on success.
     (Auto-kept on failure regardless, so the user can investigate.)
   - `--worktree-path <path>` — override the default sibling location.

2. **UX polish matching changeset's style.**

   - `version` arg is now optional.  Bare `cargo xtask release new`
     drops into a `dialoguer::Select` prompt: Patch / Minor / Major /
     Specific version (with Input prompt for the latter).
     Non-interactive run still requires the arg.
   - Plan block uses `console::style` (cyan version + branches, dim
     labels, bold version) instead of a single inline summary line.
   - Dry-run output is sectioned: fetch, worktree creation, in-worktree
     ops, PR open, cleanup — easier to follow the actual sequence.
   - Cheap validations (line, kind) happen BEFORE the fetch network
     call, so a misconfigured invocation errors instantly.

fix(federation): fix @fromContext positions for join__field (#9374)

`@fromContext` is applied to field **arguments**, so `DirectiveReferencers` stores them in `object_field_arguments` / `interface_field_arguments`. However, `needs_join_field` checks `object_fields` / `interface_fields`, causing it to miss fields that need `@join__field` with `contextArguments`.

When a field with `@fromContext` exists in all subgraphs with the same return type and no other special directives, `needs_join_field` incorrectly returned false, dropping the `@join__field` directive entirely—including the `contextArguments` data needed at runtime.

The fix maps argument positions to their parent field positions in `get_fields_with_from_context_directive`, matching the JS implementation:

```js
    // composition-js/src/merging/merge.ts:4037 — getFieldsWithFromContextDirective
    const field = application.parent.parent; // argument → field
```

https://github.com/apollographql/federation/blob/main/composition-js/src/merging/merge.ts#L4033-L4042

fix(composition): filter fake externals to only field-level `@external` (#9373)

`collect_fake_externals` traverses compound `@key` field sets (e.g., `@key(fields: "t { id }")`) and adds all reached fields to `fake_external_fields`. When a type stub uses type-level `@external` (e.g., `type T @key(fields: "id") @external { id: ID! }`), the traversal reaches `T.id` and incorrectly marks it as fake-external. This cancels out `fields_on_external_types` in `is_external()`, causing `needs_join_field()` to return false and drop all `@join__field` directives — including `external: true` — from the supergraph.

The JS implementation filters the traversal result:

```js
    collectTargetFields({...})
      .filter((field) => field.hasAppliedDirective(this.externalDirective))
      .forEach((field) => this.fakeExternalFields.add(field.coordinate));

    // federation/internals-js/src/federation.ts — collectFakeExternals, line 2709
    // https://github.com/apollographql/federation/blob/main/internals-js/src/federation.ts#L2709
```

The Rust `collect_fake_externals` was missing this filter — it added all fields from `collect_target_fields_from_field_set` unconditionally.

The fix adds `.filter(|field| external_fields.contains(field))` to only include fields that have field-level `@external` applied directly, matching the JS behavior.

fix(composition): interface cannot be a subtype of a union (#9382)

Union can only reference objects. While it is possible for a subgraph to define an `@interfaceObject` in the schema, in the merged supergraph it would still be represented as interface in the supergraph. `union_type.members` will never contain the target `interface` so the check would never succeed. `apollo-compiler` correctly validates this so we wouldn't generate invalid schema.

fix(composition): remove invalid executable directive from supergraph  (#9387)

When an executable directive has no locations common to all subgraphs, the JS composition removes it from the supergraph and returns early. The Rust implementation reported the hint but left the directive in the supergraph with zero locations and continued merging its properties.

fix(composition): fix `@interfaceObject` type kind mismatch (#9393)

`add_types_shallow` used `TypeDefinitionPosition` (a kind-carrying enum) as keys in `mismatched_types` and `subgraphs_with_interface_obj`. When a non-`@interfaceObject` subgraph was processed first, the merged schema stored `Object("Foo")` but the `@interfaceObject` map was keyed by `Interface("Foo")`, causing two lookup failures:

1. `.get()` for label lookup failed — `@interfaceObject` subgraphs were mislabeled as plain "Object Type" in `TYPE_KIND_MISMATCH` errors
2. `.contains()` for error suppression failed — a spurious `INTERFACE_OBJECT_USAGE_ERROR` was emitted

Fix: change both `mismatched_types` and `subgraphs_with_interface_obj` to use `Name` (plain type name) as keys, matching JS which uses `Set<string>` for both `mismatchedTypes` (L839) and `typesWithInterfaceObject` (L840):
https://github.com/apollographql/federation/blob/main/composition-js/src/merging/merge.ts#L838-L863

Also add early bail after `add_types_shallow` when errors exist, since type kind mismatches leave the merged schema in an inconsistent state that causes later stages to fail with internal errors that swallow the real `TYPE_KIND_MISMATCH` errors. JS avoids this by filtering mismatched types in `subgraphsTypes()` (L954-L957):
https://github.com/apollographql/federation/blob/main/composition-js/src/merging/merge.ts#L944-L961

JS `reportMismatchedTypeDefinitions` checks `isInterfaceObjectType()` directly on each source type (L929) rather than relying on a separate map lookup:
https://github.com/apollographql/federation/blob/main/composition-js/src/merging/merge.ts#L925-L942

fix(composition): drop `= {}` default when presence is inconsistent (#9389)

The Rust merger incorrectly preserved empty object defaults (`= {}`) when only some subgraphs declared them. JS composition drops the default in this case — an argument can only be optional in the supergraph if it is optional in all subgraphs.

Removes `inconsistent_defaults_are_all_coercible_empty_objects` and its special hint branch, aligning the condition with JS: `if (!isInconsistent || isIncompatible)`.

JS reference: `mergeDefaultValue` in `merge.ts`
https://github.com/apollographql/federation/blob/d4969572/composition-js/src/merging/merge.ts#L2412-L2413

`hint_on_inconsistent_value_type_field` was missing a `break` after emitting the hint. Since `report_mismatch_hint` already examines all sources internally, the loop emitted duplicate identical hints — one per subgraph missing the field.

JS breaks immediately after the first match (L1218): https://github.com/apollographql/federation/blob/main/composition-js/src/merging/merge.ts#L1189-L1221

ci: fix SIGPIPE in test-release-prep auto-tag log step

The "Log what auto-tag would do" step ran `git tag --list | head -1`
under `set -euo pipefail`.  On runners where the tag list is long
enough to fill the pipe buffer before `head` exits, `git tag` gets
SIGPIPE (exit 141), the pipeline fails, and the step fails — which
skips the downstream commit/push/PR-open steps even when the prep
itself succeeded.

Switch to `git for-each-ref --count=1`, which avoids the pipeline
entirely and is robust under pipefail.

Observed in run 26157552615 on 2.14.1.

ci: add test-auto-tag-release workflow (dry-run by default)

Introduces the auto-tagging logic in a sandboxed form, mirroring the
test-release-prep.yml pattern.  Push trigger on `main` / `main-v*`
fires automatically on every release-line merge and runs the full
target-SHA + version + idempotency logic, but logs only — does not
push the tag.

workflow_dispatch adds a `dry_run` input (default true) so we can
flip the switch from the same workflow once we trust the dry-run
output.

Safety properties: version gate (skip if no version change at the
target SHA), idempotency (skip-if-exists-at-right-SHA, error-if-at-
wrong-SHA), SIGPIPE-safe parsing.

Graduation later: rename to auto-tag-release.yml and drop the dry-run
guard.

Changelog pre-prep: recategorize dedup cache fast path as maintenance

The dedup-cache fast path change is an internal performance optimization
(no new API, no new config) — `perf(cache):` in the source commit, not
`feat(cache):`.  Filing it under `feat_*` causes it to land in the
Features section of the changelog, which is misleading for a patch
release.

Rename to `maint_*` so it lands under Maintenance with the other
internal-improvement entries.

Add @apollographql/graphos as co-codeowner of OL/runtime-readiness paths

CODEOWNERS treats multiple owners as any-can-approve.  Adding GraphOS

fix(redis): subscribe to connect events before connect_pool to avoid startup hang

When `required_to_start: true` and Redis is unreachable, `create_client_pool`
called `connect_pool()` and then `wait_for_connect().await`. fred's
`wait_for_connect` subscribes to the connect broadcast channel at the moment
it is awaited; if fred's bounded reconnect policy exhausted its 15 attempts
before the subscription was registered, the terminal `broadcast_connect(Err)`
fired into the void and the subscriber waited forever for an event that
would never come. This surfaced as a 120s timeout on
`connection_failure_blocks_startup` on contended CI runners (CircleCI runs
369728 and 369751).

Mirror fred's own `Pool::init` shape: collect per-client connect-notification
receivers before calling `connect_pool()`, then await each receiver in turn.
The per-client `ConnectHandle`s needed by the watcher task remain unchanged.

Verified with 10x local stress on the redis test (10/10 pass) plus the full
integration::redis::* group (19/19 pass) and the
cache::redis::test_against_redis unit suite (39/39 pass).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(cache): wrap recv() in inner loop so Lagged retries on the same rx

The previous code's `Lagged` arm used `continue` directly inside the
`match`, but the innermost loop was the outer `for mut rx in
connect_rxs`. `continue` therefore advanced to the next receiver and
dropped the lagged one, skipping verification of that client's
connect event entirely. Under the documented `required_to_start`
contract this silently weakens the fail-fast guarantee: in the worst
case every rx lags and the function returns Ok without observing any
successful connect.

Wrap the match in an inner `loop { ... }` so `Lagged`'s `continue`
re-awaits on the same rx, which matches the comment's intent.

after a hard-coded `tokio::sleep(3000ms)`. This was racing on two axes:

v2.14.2-rc.0 can be cut without manual local steps, while keeping the
apollo-bot2 PAT exposure narrow.

What's new:

  (e.g., `2.14.2-rc.0`), so existing `[execute]` flow keeps working for
  RC sandboxes too.

  the dispatched branch as apollo-bot2 — no separate prep PR, since
  there's nothing for a reviewer to look at beyond version bumps.
- Final-release path is unchanged: fresh prep branch, open PR for
  reviewers to eyeball CHANGELOG entries.

Exposure tightening:

- Checkout step is now `persist-credentials: false` — apollo-bot2's
  PAT is no longer baked into the local git remote URL for the full
  workflow run.
- The only step that touches the PAT directly is the push step that
  needs write access to the protected release branch.  PAT is in env
  for that step alone and is used in a one-shot remote URL — never
  written to `.git/config`.
- Same tightening applied to the final-release prep-branch push for
  consistency (workflow token via inline URL when PAT isn't set).

fix(composition, query-planning): Refactor code for `@link` to address some long-standing issues/todos (#9569)

This PR does the following:
1. It refactors a part of the `@link` code to adhere to current conventions/code structure, specifically:
    - Moves logic for parsing GraphQL AST into link-related data structures (and vice versa) into `link_spec_definition.rs`, to better reflect how other `*_spec_definition.rs` files are structured. (These were largely moved into `TryFrom`s/`From`s.)
    - Moves link-related constants/names into  `link_spec_definition.rs` and renames them, to better reflect how other `*_spec_definition.rs` files are structured.
    - Moves `is_bootstrap_directive()` (and downstream functions) into `link_spec_definition.rs`, as it's really a question about link spec semantics.
    - Creates a file `metadata.rs` for `LinksMetadata` and its impls, and moves `links_metadata()` into the method `LinksMetadata::from_schema()` to better reflect conventions.
    - Deletes `database.rs`, as all logic has been moved out of it, and the name has become confusing/reflects concepts in the far past that we've moved away from.
    - Creates a file `spec_registry.rs` to contain `SpecRegistry` and its impls. It also contains the static helper methods for `Identity` that give the identity for each known spec.
 2. It replaces `LinkError` and `SpecError` with `FederationError`. They're ancient error enums that were introduced in early versions of the codebase, and they'd inadvertently caused error messages to be worded awkwardly in the form `phrase 1: phrase 2: phrase 3` instead of a single, plain english sentence (the phrases were also somewhat redundant). They've been replaced with the federation errors they translate to, and the messages have been cleaned up to be single sentences that always include some value from the schema.
    - Not all error messages have been cleaned up; some parts have been left to a follow-up PR focusing on `@link` validation. 
    - Note that this approach still has some non-ideal parts to it. The error messages assume they're dealing with `@link`, but it's possible they're dealing with `@core` or a renamed `@link` instead (these cases are rare). This is a general problem across the codebase though, and is more an issue of downstream validations not having quite enough context (or inversely, upstream callers not getting downstream errors in the right structure).
4. A part of `links_metadata()` (now `LinksMetadata::from_schema()`) was editing `@link`s for Fed 1 to contain a specific set of imports. Based on the callsites, it's unclear why this was happening (other folks don't seem to know why either, and it wasn't in the JS's equivalent class `CoreFeatures`). The JS doesn't even declare a fed 1.0 spec (since fed 1 subgraphs were before we introduced the concept of `@core`/`@link`). I've accordingly removed the logic for that in `links_metadata()`, and removed Fed 1 from `FEDERATION_VERSIONS`.
5. The logic for creating `Link`s from `Directive`s (now in `Link::try_from(value: &Directive)`) had some issues that are now fixed:

`merge_enum_value` built `pos_sources` by mapping over every subgraph that declared the enum *type*, rather than only the subgraphs that define the specific value. * test(persisted-queries): cover per-client freeform safelist scoping

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(persisted-queries): respect manifest client-name scope in freeform safelist

Freeform (body-based) safelist matching normalized the manifest into a
body -> operation_id map, dropping each operation's client_name. Matching was
therefore body-only, while ID-based lookup keys on (operation_id, client_name).
An operation registered for one client was accepted for any client.

Give the freeform safelist a client-name dimension
(body -> {client_name -> operation_id}) and thread the request's client name
into the match, preferring an exact client match and falling back to a
client-agnostic (None) entry, mirroring get_operation_body. This also fixes a
latent collision where two entries sharing a body under different client names
clobbered each other nondeterministically. Client-name resolution is factored
into a shared helper used by both the ID and freeform paths.

clientName is a self-reported, unauthenticated header, so this is a
correctness/consistency fix rather than an authorization boundary.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* refactor(persisted-queries): key freeform safelist on a struct instead of nested maps

Address review feedback on the freeform safelist representation. Replace the
nested `HashMap<body, HashMap<client_name, operation_id>>` with a flat
`HashMap<NormalizedBodyKey, String>` keyed on a `(normalized_body, client_name)`
struct, and pull the per-client lookup into a `get_pq_id_for_normalized_body`
helper. Behavior is unchanged: prefer an exact client-name match, then fall
back to a client-agnostic (`None`) entry.

When applying `@join__field`, the `Merger` tries to limit applications to those where it adds information to the supergraph. When a field does not have `@join__field`, it is assumed to be present in all subgraphs. There are some cases where we add more applications than necessary. Instead of of changing the merge logic to be more selective, we can prune the schema after all merges are complete to remove this pattern. fix(composition): restrict usage of auth directives on interfaces (#8826)

Restricts usage of `@authenticated`, `@policy` and `@requiresScopes` from being applied on interfaces, interface objects and their fields.

GraphQL spec currently does not define any interface inheritance rules and developers have to explicitly redefine all interface fields on their implementations. At runtime, GraphQL servers cannot return abstract types and always return concrete output types. Due to the above, applying auth directives on the interfaces may lead to unexpected runtime behavior as they won't have any effect at runtime.

fix(composition): fix directive arg merging logic (#8878)

Update `merge_applied_directives` to explicitly compare directive application arguments (accounting for default argument values) without modifying original directive. Previous logic was explicitly modifying original directive application and always populating it with default arg values even if they were not specified by the user, i.e. given a subgraph

```graphql
type Query {
  foo: String @deprecated
}
```

We expect the supergraph to also define it as

```graphql
type Query {
  # previous logic was applying @deprecated(reason: "No longer supported")
  foo: String @deprecated
}
```

fix(composition): enforce transitive auth requirements (#8870)

Adds new `validate_transitive_access_control_requirements_in_the_supergraph` post merge validation check to ensure that all fields that depends on data from other parts of the supergraph through `@requires` and/or `@fromContext` directives explicitly specify matching `@authenticated`, `@requiresScopes` and/or `@policy` auth requirements, e.g.

```graphql
type T @key(fields: "id") {
  id: ID!
  extra: String @external
  # we need explicit @authenticated as it is needed to access extra
  requiresExtra: String @requires(fields: "extra") @authenticated
}

type T @key(fields: "id") {
  id: ID!
  extra: String @authenticated
}
```

* fixed `validate_override` logic
* fixed `validate_field_sharing` logic to use correct source

fix(composition): handle missing directive definitions for older fed versions (#9229)

`SpecDefinition::directive_definition()` errors when a directive name resolves through the federation link prefix but the definition doesn't exist in the schema. This happens for directives added in newer federation versions (e.g. `@policy` in v2.6, `@fromContext` in v2.8) when subgraphs use an older version like v2.5.

The JS implementation avoids this by returning a stub with empty `applications()` from `getPost20FederationDirective`. The Rust code now uses `directive_name_in_schema` with a soft lookup in `directive_definitions`, gracefully skipping directives that don't exist in the subgraph schema.

fix(to-api-schema): Revert reorder of searching for imports vs fully qualified names when computing source feature (#9244)

In #9164, the code for `source_link_of_type()` and `source_link_of_directive()` was changed to be more in line with the JS equivalent `sourceFeature()`. As part of that, the methods were altered to attempt parsing the name as a fully qualified name before attempting to search through imports, as the JS code does. In JS these functions are only really used by composition, and flipping the order did cause a previously-ignored Rust composition test (ported from JS) to start passing.

However, in Rust, the `source_link_of_type()` and `source_link_of_directive()` are **_not_** only used by composition; the `to_api_schema()` function uses both of these methods (and in doing so, diverges from the JS implementation). And for the Rust implementation to properly handle specific edge cases around imports, it needs `source_link_of_type()` and `source_link_of_directive()` to search for imports before parsing the name as a fully qualified name.

So this PR reverts specifically just the ordering change made in #9164 to imports vs fully qualified names (the rest of the fixes in that PR remain in effect). Part of that means re-ignoring the aforementioned composition test; this will be fixed in a later PR.

xtask: add `release status` and `release reconcile` (milestone 1)

Adds two new `cargo xtask release` subcommands that read release state
from git remotes + GitHub and automate the most mechanical piece of the
flow (the reconcile-main-back-to-dev PR).  The RELEASE_CHECKLIST.md
stays as the "star map" documenting what the xtask does and serves as
the manual escape hatch when tooling is unavailable.

## `cargo xtask release status`

Read-only state detector.  Groups branches into release lines (tip =
plain `main`/`dev`, LTS = `main-v<MAJ>.<MIN>.x` + `dev-v<MAJ>.<MIN>.x`
pairs), attributes version branches/tags/PRs to the right line, and
prints a per-line snapshot of in-flight work.  Flags: `--repo`,
`--origin`, `--line`, `--json`, `--no-fetch`, `--non-interactive`.

## `cargo xtask release reconcile --version <X.Y.Z>`

Automates RELEASE_CHECKLIST.md §Reconciling steps 1-9.  Infers the
release line from `--line` or the current git branch (falls back to
interactive prompt).  Creates `reconcile-v<VERSION>`, merges line-dev
into it with a pre-seeded commit message (so no-conflict and
with-conflict paths both produce valid commits), pushes, opens the PR,
and sets auto-merge.  On merge conflicts it stops with instructions to
resolve locally and re-run with `--resume`.  Also supports
`--no-auto-merge` and `--dry-run`.

## Shared infrastructure

- `xtask/src/gh.rs` — consolidated `gh` CLI helper (`available`,
  `token`, `run`, `json`).  Extracted from ad-hoc calls in
  `changeset/mod.rs`; that module is migrated to consume the shared
  helper in the same change.
- `xtask/src/lib.rs` — new `git\!` and `git_out\!` macros matching the
  existing `cargo\!` / `npm\!` pattern.
- `xtask/src/commands/release/` — old `release.rs` split into
  `mod.rs`, `common.rs` (shared args + branch/line parsing),
  `prepare.rs`, `pre_verify.rs`, `state.rs` (detection), `status.rs`,
  `reconcile.rs`.

## LTS/security support is first-class from day one

Every subcommand accepts `--repo` (target GitHub repo, for private
forks), `--origin` (git remote), and `--line` (tip or
`<MAJ>.<MIN>.x`).  The `Line` type + branch-name regex are the single
source of truth for "which main/dev pair are we talking about" —
versions and tags are attributed back to lines automatically.

## RELEASE_CHECKLIST.md

Points readers to `release status` at the top of §Building a Release
and to `release reconcile` at the top of §Reconciling.  All manual
steps stay as-is — they're what the xtask runs under the hood.

xtask: recognize pre-release staging lines + --no-fetch warning

Follow-ups surfaced from running `release status` against real router
state.

## Staging line support (`dev-v3.x`)

Adds a new `Line::Staging { major }` variant alongside Tip and Lts.
Matches `main-v<MAJ>.x` / `dev-v<MAJ>.x` branches — a pre-release line
for a future major before any minor has been chosen.  Typical shape:
solo dev branch (`dev-v3.x`) accepting alpha releases, no main
counterpart yet because no release has shipped.

Also widens `--line` flag accepts `3.x`, version attribution splits
claims correctly between Tip/Staging/Lts (a 2.10.5 tag belongs to the
2.10.x LTS; a 3.0.0-alpha.0 tag belongs to the 3.x staging line; a
2.15.0 tag belongs to tip because nothing else claims 2.15).

## --no-fetch staleness warning

When `status --no-fetch` is passed against a stale clone, the tool used
to quietly report "no in-progress" for lines that actually had active
PRs.  Now prints a header reminder:

  Release state — apollographql/router (origin)
    (local state — did not `git fetch`; pass without --no-fetch for fresh data)

Easy to miss if you're running in CI; loud enough to notice interactively.

## JSON output

Adds `is_staging` field alongside existing `is_lts`.

fix(composition): prevent EnumTypeUsage from downgrading Both to Input/Output (#9303)

The `track_enum_usage` match arms for `Input | Both` and `Output | Both` incorrectly collapsed the `Both` variant back to a single-position usage whenever a subsequent field referenced the same enum in an already-seen position. For example, the sequence Input → Both → Output (third field) would overwrite `Both` with `Output`, silently skipping ENUM_VALUE_MISMATCH validation for enums used in both input and output contexts.

The JS composer (`merge.ts:2206`) handles this correctly: once position reaches `'Both'`, the expression `existing.position !== thisPosition` is always true, so `Both` is preserved.

The fix adds an explicit early match arm that returns `Both` unchanged, and removes the `| Both` alternatives from the `Input` and `Output` arms. This aligns RS behavior with JS for ~1,800 real-world supergraphs from the federation performance harness (groups 3.8 and 3.9).

feat(composition): preserve hints on composition failure (#9305)

Previously, when composition failed (either during merge or satisfiability validation), all WARN-level hints were silently discarded because the error type `Vec<CompositionError>` had no room for them.

Introduce `CompositionFailure { errors, hints }` as the error type for `merge_subgraphs`, `validate_satisfiability`, `compose`, and related functions. This preserves `INCONSISTENT_*` warnings, `UNUSED_ENUM_TYPE`, `OVERRIDDEN_FIELD_CAN_BE_REMOVED`, and other hints alongside errors on all failure paths:

- `merge_subgraphs`: carries merge hints when merge produces errors
- `validate_satisfiability`: carries accumulated hints when satisfiability fails
- `validate_satisfiability_with_connectors`: merges hints from both merge and satisfiability phases, sanitizes connector names in both
- `compose` / `compose_with_connectors`: propagates hints through the full pipeline; pre-merge phases (no hints) convert via `From<Vec<CompositionError>>`

xtask: isolate `release new` in a git worktree + style the UX

Two structural changes to `cargo xtask release new`:

1. **WorkTree isolation.**  All destructive git ops (branch creation,
   empty-commit shim, push) now run inside an isolated `git worktree`
   sibling to the project root.  The user's primary checkout HEAD,
   index, and working tree are NOT touched.  Concurrent runs each get
   their own worktree — no race on shared .git/index state.

   New helper at `xtask/src/worktree.rs`:
   - `WorkTree::create(path, base_ref)` — creates the worktree.
   - `.git(args)` / `.git_out(args)` — run git inside it.
   - Drop impl removes the worktree (`git worktree remove --force`).
   - `.keep()` opts out of cleanup for post-mortem debugging.

   New flags on `release new`:
   - `--keep-worktree` — keep the worktree directory on success.
     (Auto-kept on failure regardless, so the user can investigate.)
   - `--worktree-path <path>` — override the default sibling location.

2. **UX polish matching changeset's style.**

   - `version` arg is now optional.  Bare `cargo xtask release new`
     drops into a `dialoguer::Select` prompt: Patch / Minor / Major /
     Specific version (with Input prompt for the latter).
     Non-interactive run still requires the arg.
   - Plan block uses `console::style` (cyan version + branches, dim
     labels, bold version) instead of a single inline summary line.
   - Dry-run output is sectioned: fetch, worktree creation, in-worktree
     ops, PR open, cleanup — easier to follow the actual sequence.
   - Cheap validations (line, kind) happen BEFORE the fetch network
     call, so a misconfigured invocation errors instantly.

fix(federation): fix @fromContext positions for join__field (#9374)

`@fromContext` is applied to field **arguments**, so `DirectiveReferencers` stores them in `object_field_arguments` / `interface_field_arguments`. However, `needs_join_field` checks `object_fields` / `interface_fields`, causing it to miss fields that need `@join__field` with `contextArguments`.

When a field with `@fromContext` exists in all subgraphs with the same return type and no other special directives, `needs_join_field` incorrectly returned false, dropping the `@join__field` directive entirely—including the `contextArguments` data needed at runtime.

The fix maps argument positions to their parent field positions in `get_fields_with_from_context_directive`, matching the JS implementation:

```js
    // composition-js/src/merging/merge.ts:4037 — getFieldsWithFromContextDirective
    const field = application.parent.parent; // argument → field
```

https://github.com/apollographql/federation/blob/main/composition-js/src/merging/merge.ts#L4033-L4042

fix(composition): filter fake externals to only field-level `@external` (#9373)

`collect_fake_externals` traverses compound `@key` field sets (e.g., `@key(fields: "t { id }")`) and adds all reached fields to `fake_external_fields`. When a type stub uses type-level `@external` (e.g., `type T @key(fields: "id") @external { id: ID! }`), the traversal reaches `T.id` and incorrectly marks it as fake-external. This cancels out `fields_on_external_types` in `is_external()`, causing `needs_join_field()` to return false and drop all `@join__field` directives — including `external: true` — from the supergraph.

The JS implementation filters the traversal result:

```js
    collectTargetFields({...})
      .filter((field) => field.hasAppliedDirective(this.externalDirective))
      .forEach((field) => this.fakeExternalFields.add(field.coordinate));

    // federation/internals-js/src/federation.ts — collectFakeExternals, line 2709
    // https://github.com/apollographql/federation/blob/main/internals-js/src/federation.ts#L2709
```

The Rust `collect_fake_externals` was missing this filter — it added all fields from `collect_target_fields_from_field_set` unconditionally.

The fix adds `.filter(|field| external_fields.contains(field))` to only include fields that have field-level `@external` applied directly, matching the JS behavior.

fix(composition): interface cannot be a subtype of a union (#9382)

Union can only reference objects. While it is possible for a subgraph to define an `@interfaceObject` in the schema, in the merged supergraph it would still be represented as interface in the supergraph. `union_type.members` will never contain the target `interface` so the check would never succeed. `apollo-compiler` correctly validates this so we wouldn't generate invalid schema.

This PR cleans this incorrect logic but it should have no effect on the merged supergraph (this check would always fail).

Allowing unions to include interfaces/other unions is an old issue (https://github.com/graphql/graphql-spec/issues/711) and it looks like it won't be tackled anytime soon.

fix(composition): remove invalid executable directive from supergraph  (#9387)

When an executable directive has no locations common to all subgraphs, the JS composition removes it from the supergraph and returns early. The Rust implementation reported the hint but left the directive in the supergraph with zero locations and continued merging its properties.

This adds `dest.remove()` and an early return to match the JS behavior, preventing an invalid directive definition with empty locations from appearing in the supergraph.

fix(composition): fix `@interfaceObject` type kind mismatch (#9393)

`add_types_shallow` used `TypeDefinitionPosition` (a kind-carrying enum) as keys in `mismatched_types` and `subgraphs_with_interface_obj`. When a non-`@interfaceObject` subgraph was processed first, the merged schema stored `Object("Foo")` but the `@interfaceObject` map was keyed by `Interface("Foo")`, causing two lookup failures:

1. `.get()` for label lookup failed — `@interfaceObject` subgraphs were mislabeled as plain "Object Type" in `TYPE_KIND_MISMATCH` errors
2. `.contains()` for error suppression failed — a spurious `INTERFACE_OBJECT_USAGE_ERROR` was emitted

Fix: change both `mismatched_types` and `subgraphs_with_interface_obj` to use `Name` (plain type name) as keys, matching JS which uses `Set<string>` for both `mismatchedTypes` (L839) and `typesWithInterfaceObject` (L840):
https://github.com/apollographql/federation/blob/main/composition-js/src/merging/merge.ts#L838-L863

Also add early bail after `add_types_shallow` when errors exist, since type kind mismatches leave the merged schema in an inconsistent state that causes later stages to fail with internal errors that swallow the real `TYPE_KIND_MISMATCH` errors. JS avoids this by filtering mismatched types in `subgraphsTypes()` (L954-L957):
https://github.com/apollographql/federation/blob/main/composition-js/src/merging/merge.ts#L944-L961

JS `reportMismatchedTypeDefinitions` checks `isInterfaceObjectType()` directly on each source type (L929) rather than relying on a separate map lookup:
https://github.com/apollographql/federation/blob/main/composition-js/src/merging/merge.ts#L925-L942

fix(composition): drop `= {}` default when presence is inconsistent (#9389)

The Rust merger incorrectly preserved empty object defaults (`= {}`) when only some subgraphs declared them. JS composition drops the default in this case — an argument can only be optional in the supergraph if it is optional in all subgraphs.

Removes `inconsistent_defaults_are_all_coercible_empty_objects` and its special hint branch, aligning the condition with JS: `if (!isInconsistent || isIncompatible)`.

JS reference: `mergeDefaultValue` in `merge.ts`
https://github.com/apollographql/federation/blob/d4969572/composition-js/src/merging/merge.ts#L2412-L2413

fix(composition): add early return in `hint_on_inconsistent_value_type_field` (#9395)

`hint_on_inconsistent_value_type_field` was missing a `break` after emitting the hint. Since `report_mismatch_hint` already examines all sources internally, the loop emitted duplicate identical hints — one per subgraph missing the field.

JS breaks immediately after the first match (L1218): https://github.com/apollographql/federation/blob/main/composition-js/src/merging/merge.ts#L1189-L1221

fix(composition): Add early return in `hint_on_inconsistent_output_enum_value` (#9394)

`hint_on_inconsistent_output_enum_value` was missing a `return` after emitting the hint. Since `report_mismatch_hint` already examines all sources internally, the loop emitted duplicate identical hints — one per subgraph missing the value.

JS returns immediately after the first match (L2732): https://github.com/apollographql/federation/blob/main/composition-js/src/merging/merge.ts#L2713-L2735

The existing comment on L260 ("As soon as we find a subgraph that has the type but not the member, we hint") already described the intended behavior — the `return` was simply missing.

fix(composition): emit fallback `SubgraphLocation` when AST has no source (#9436)

`Subgraph::node_locations` returned an empty `Vec` when a schema node lacked AST source location data (common after programmatic schema modifications during the upgrade step). This caused `report_mismatch` to omit subgraphs from the `locations` array, leading to incorrect `maybe_prepend_subgraph` prefix behavior.

With only one subgraph in locations, a `[subgraph]` prefix was added to the message; JS included all subgraphs (2+), so no prefix was added. The message bodies were identical but the prefix differed.

Now `node_locations` produces a fallback `SubgraphLocation` with a default range (`0:0..0:0`) when no source data exists, matching JS behavior. This resolves mismatches in `INCONSISTENT_ENTITY`, `INCONSISTENT_INTERFACE_VALUE_TYPE_FIELD`, and
`INCONSISTENT_OBJECT_VALUE_TYPE_FIELD` hints.

ci: fix SIGPIPE in test-release-prep auto-tag log step

The "Log what auto-tag would do" step ran `git tag --list | head -1`
under `set -euo pipefail`.  On runners where the tag list is long
enough to fill the pipe buffer before `head` exits, `git tag` gets
SIGPIPE (exit 141), the pipeline fails, and the step fails — which
skips the downstream commit/push/PR-open steps even when the prep
itself succeeded.

Switch to `git for-each-ref --count=1`, which avoids the pipeline
entirely and is robust under pipefail.

Observed in run 26157552615 on 2.14.1.

test-release-prep.yml pattern.  Push trigger on `main` / `main-v*`
fires automatically on every release-line merge and runs the full

push the tag.

Safety properties: version gate (skip if no version change at the

fix(redis): subscribe to connect events before connect_pool to avoid startup hang

When `required_to_start: true` and Redis is unreachable, `create_client_pool`
called `connect_pool()` and then `wait_for_connect().await`. fred's
`wait_for_connect` subscribes to the connect broadcast channel at the moment
it is awaited; if fred's bounded reconnect policy exhausted its 15 attempts
before the subscription was registered, the terminal `broadcast_connect(Err)`
fired into the void and the subscriber waited forever for an event that
would never come. This surfaced as a 120s timeout on
`connection_failure_blocks_startup` on contended CI runners (CircleCI runs
369728 and 369751).

Mirror fred's own `Pool::init` shape: collect per-client connect-notification
receivers before calling `connect_pool()`, then await each receiver in turn.
The per-client `ConnectHandle`s needed by the watcher task remain unchanged.

Verified with 10x local stress on the redis test (10/10 pass) plus the full
integration::redis::* group (19/19 pass) and the
cache::redis::test_against_redis unit suite (39/39 pass).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(cache): wrap recv() in inner loop so Lagged retries on the same rx

The previous code's `Lagged` arm used `continue` directly inside the
`match`, but the innermost loop was the outer `for mut rx in
connect_rxs`. `continue` therefore advanced to the next receiver and
dropped the lagged one, skipping verification of that client's
connect event entirely. Under the documented `required_to_start`
contract this silently weakens the fail-fast guarantee: in the worst
case every rx lags and the function returns Ok without observing any
successful connect.

Wrap the match in an inner `loop { ... }` so `Lagged`'s `continue`
re-awaits on the same rx, which matches the comment's intent.

test(entity_cache): stabilize test_cache_error_metrics (Pattern B+C)

The test asserted an exact metric value (`} 1`) for
`apollo_router_cache_redis_errors_total{error_type="io",kind="entity"}`
after a hard-coded `tokio::sleep(3000ms)`. This was racing on two axes:

  1. The 3 s sleep was a "guess" of when the metric pipeline would have
     observed the first error. Too short and the metric is still 0; too
     long is wasteful.
  2. The error counter is incremented per failed Redis op (connect,
     query, client event, heartbeat). With 3 queries, fred's connect
     retry loop, and the 100 ms `metrics_interval`, the actual count
     can be 1, 2, 3, or more — none of which the test could predict.

Replace with `assert_metric_non_zero`, which already polls up to 15 s
and matches any positive value. This is the same pattern used by
`test_redis_emits_configuration_error_metric` (redis.rs) for the same
metric family. The semantic the test actually wants ("Redis IO errors
are recorded when Redis is unreachable") is preserved; the brittle
exact-count coupling is removed.

Verified 30/30 passing locally, run times ~3.4-4.1 s (down from the
prior 4-5 s+ floor introduced by the mandatory 3 s sleep).

ci(release-prep): add pre-release path, scope apollo-bot2 PAT exposure

Adds pre-release support to the release-prep workflow so an RC like
v2.14.2-rc.0 can be cut without manual local steps, while keeping the
apollo-bot2 PAT exposure narrow.

What's new:

- New `pre_release` workflow_dispatch input (boolean, default false).
  When true, the workflow passes `--pre-release` to `cargo xtask release
  prepare`, which skips CHANGELOG generation and only bumps versions.
- Push-trigger sandbox auto-detects pre-release from the version suffix
  (e.g., `2.14.2-rc.0`), so existing `[execute]` flow keeps working for
  RC sandboxes too.
- Pre-release path commits the version bump and pushes it directly to
  the dispatched branch as apollo-bot2 — no separate prep PR, since
  there's nothing for a reviewer to look at beyond version bumps.
- Final-release path is unchanged: fresh prep branch, open PR for
  reviewers to eyeball CHANGELOG entries.

Exposure tightening:

- Checkout step is now `persist-credentials: false` — apollo-bot2's
  PAT is no longer baked into the local git remote URL for the full
  workflow run.
- The only step that touches the PAT directly is the push step that
  needs write access to the protected release branch.  PAT is in env
  for that step alone and is used in a one-shot remote URL — never
  written to `.git/config`.
- Same tightening applied to the final-release prep-branch push for
  consistency (workflow token via inline URL when PAT isn't set).

label, which is already applied at PR-create time by `test-release-new.yml`.

fix(composition): fix order-dependent executable directive location intersection (#9548)

The executable directive location intersection used `Vec::is_empty()` to detect both "not yet initialized" and "empty intersection result". When the first subgraph (alphabetically) had no executable locations, the second subgraph's locations were treated as initialization instead of being intersected with the empty set — leaking the directive into the supergraph.

Use `Option<Vec>` to distinguish "not initialized" from "empty intersection", making the result order-independent.

When filling in missing `@interfaceObject` fields on implementation types, the code blindly called `merge_applied_directive` for ALL access control directives with empty sources. The DNF conjunction merger then produced `@policy(policies: [])` from zero applications.

Fix the call site to only merge access control directives when `access_control_additional_sources` has entries for the target field, matching JS behavior at:
https://github.com/apollographql/federation/blob/8200b154/composition-js/src/merging/merge.ts#L1455

Also add a safety-net early return in `merge_applied_directive` when `directive_counts` is empty (zero applications from all sources), matching JS at:

fix(composition, query-planning): Refactor code for `@link` to address some long-standing issues/todos (#9569)

This PR does the following:
1. It refactors a part of the `@link` code to adhere to current conventions/code structure, specifically:
    - Moves logic for parsing GraphQL AST into link-related data structures (and vice versa) into `link_spec_definition.rs`, to better reflect how other `*_spec_definition.rs` files are structured. (These were largely moved into `TryFrom`s/`From`s.)
    - Moves link-related constants/names into  `link_spec_definition.rs` and renames them, to better reflect how other `*_spec_definition.rs` files are structured.
    - Moves `is_bootstrap_directive()` (and downstream functions) into `link_spec_definition.rs`, as it's really a question about link spec semantics.
    - Creates a file `metadata.rs` for `LinksMetadata` and its impls, and moves `links_metadata()` into the method `LinksMetadata::from_schema()` to better reflect conventions.
    - Deletes `database.rs`, as all logic has been moved out of it, and the name has become confusing/reflects concepts in the far past that we've moved away from.
    - Creates a file `spec_registry.rs` to contain `SpecRegistry` and its impls. It also contains the static helper methods for `Identity` that give the identity for each known spec.
 2. It replaces `LinkError` and `SpecError` with `FederationError`. They're ancient error enums that were introduced in early versions of the codebase, and they'd inadvertently caused error messages to be worded awkwardly in the form `phrase 1: phrase 2: phrase 3` instead of a single, plain english sentence (the phrases were also somewhat redundant). They've been replaced with the federation errors they translate to, and the messages have been cleaned up to be single sentences that always include some value from the schema.
    - Not all error messages have been cleaned up; some parts have been left to a follow-up PR focusing on `@link` validation. 
    - Note that this approach still has some non-ideal parts to it. The error messages assume they're dealing with `@link`, but it's possible they're dealing with `@core` or a renamed `@link` instead (these cases are rare). This is a general problem across the codebase though, and is more an issue of downstream validations not having quite enough context (or inversely, upstream callers not getting downstream errors in the right structure).
4. A part of `links_metadata()` (now `LinksMetadata::from_schema()`) was editing `@link`s for Fed 1 to contain a specific set of imports. Based on the callsites, it's unclear why this was happening (other folks don't seem to know why either, and it wasn't in the JS's equivalent class `CoreFeatures`). The JS doesn't even declare a fed 1.0 spec (since fed 1 subgraphs were before we introduced the concept of `@core`/`@link`). I've accordingly removed the logic for that in `links_metadata()`, and removed Fed 1 from `FEDERATION_VERSIONS`.
5. The logic for creating `Link`s from `Directive`s (now in `Link::try_from(value: &Directive)`) had some issues that are now fixed:
    - If the spec alias/`as` argument were not a string, it previously didn't error.
    - If the purpose/`for` argument were null, it would previously error.
    - If the `import` argument were not a list, it would be previously be treated as an empty list, while GraphQL spec says it should be coerced into a list of size one.
6. The `Display` impls for link-related data structures were (in some cases) manually printing GraphQL syntax. In those cases, we now instead have `From`s to convert the data structures to GraphQL AST, and then just print the AST.

fix(composition): seed shallow directive definitions with name only (#9595)

`Merger::add_directives_shallow` seeded the merged schema with the first subgraph's full directive definition (arguments included) via `insert(definition.clone())`. The per-directive merge step (`merge_custom_core_directive` / `merge_executable_directive_definition`) only inserts missing arguments and never removes pre-seeded ones, so the merged definition accumulated the union of arguments across subgraphs that define the same composed directive with differing signatures — diverging from JS, which derives the argument set solely from the selected source definition.

Mirror JS `addDirectivesShallow` (`new DirectiveDefinition(name)`) by seeding a name-only definition; arguments, locations, repeatability, and description are populated later by the per-directive merge step.

fix(composition): only merge enum-value directives from subgraphs that define the value (#9598)

`merge_enum_value` built `pos_sources` by mapping over every subgraph that declared the enum *type*, rather than only the subgraphs that define the specific value. Those extra sources were then passed to `merge_description` and `record_applied_directives_to_merge`, making subgraphs that omit the value appear as if they applied the value's directives with empty arguments.

The visible symptom was a polluted INCONSISTENT_NON_REPEATABLE_DIRECTIVE_ARGUMENTS hint: for an inconsistent `@deprecated` application on an enum value, the message listed every subgraph that merely declares the enum (including ones that don't define the value) instead of only the subgraph(s) that actually define it. This diverged from the JS composer, which lists only the defining subgraph(s).

Gate `pos_sources` on `enum_type.values.contains_key(value_name)`, matching the existing `value_sources` gating a few lines above. Adds a regression test that composes an enum whose value is defined in only some subgraphs with inconsistent `@deprecated` arguments and asserts the hint omits the non-defining subgraph.

Adds `coerce_argument_directive_application_values` helper and calls it in both the object and interface field loops within `coerce_schema_values`.

fix: skip `@requires` field set validation during fed v1 schema upgrade (backport 2.16) (#9894)

During fed v1 → fed v2 upgrade, `fix_inactive_provides_and_requires` calls `remove_inactive_requires_and_provides_from_subgraph` with a clone of the subgraph as the "supergraph". This causes `@requires` field sets with inline fragment type conditions (e.g. `... on Pet`) to fail validation when the type condition is only valid cross-subgraph (the subgraph defines unrelated interfaces, but another subgraph has a type implementing both).

The fix adds a `FieldSetValidation` enum (`Validate`/`Skip`) to `parse_field_set_without_normalization` and threads it through `remove_inactive_requires_and_provides_from_subgraph`. The upgrade path passes `Skip` since the real supergraph isn't available yet — full validation happens later during post-merge against the merged supergraph. The supergraph extraction path continues to pass `Validate`.

Backport of https://github.com/apollographql/router/pull/9722

fix(composition): Field merging wrongly declares a nullable type is a subtype of a non-null supertype (backport 2.16) (#9896)

This PR fixes a bug in composition, where field merging may decide that a nullable type is a subtype of a non-null supertype due to a bug in `Merger::is_strict_subtype()`.

This bug is a regression compared to Javascript composition behavior, and can cause runtime errors if such composed supergraph schemas make it to router, so we should backport it to LTS `2.16`.
